comments.body: The 28 op-cert tests are moved into `.github/windows-sweep-deselect/openssh-key-acl.args` by the almondy-columned-iguanodon change (5888f4941be, pending Gerrit). That change also adds the non-gating `icacls` step to the Windows sweep, which prints the ACL of a fresh key's folder, the key, and a fresh `tempfile.mkdtemp()` directory.

compiled_state.description:
## Observation
In the scheduled Windows sweep at `b4e0d01b649` (2026-11-15/16), `tests/unit/test_opcert_privkey_env_pop_932d.py::test_compose_still_works_after_pop` failed in `rebar.opcert_service.keyprov.compose_signer`: `OpcertKeyError: the op-cert key is malformed, encrypted (passphrase-protected), or otherwise unusable: Bad permissions. Try removing permissions for user: \OWNER RIGHTS (S-1-3-4) on file C:/Users/RUNN...`. That test supplies the key inline, so it never reaches rebar's own mode check; the refusal comes from `ssh-keygen -y` (`src/rebar/opcert_service/keyprov.py:131-151`), which validates the copy `compose_signer` writes into a `tempfile.mkdtemp()` directory (`keyprov.py:67-74`).

Win32-OpenSSH's key permission check accepts only the file owner, SYSTEM and Administrators. The copy's ACL carries an OWNER RIGHTS ACE. Every `compose_signer` path writes the same kind of copy, so once rebar's POSIX mode check is skipped on Windows (almondy-columned-iguanodon) the 30 op-cert tests in `.github/windows-sweep-deselect/openssh-key-acl.args` are expected to stop here.

## Hypotheses (unproven)
- The OWNER RIGHTS ACE comes from Python 3.13's `os.mkdir(mode=0o700)` on Windows (used by `tempfile.mkdtemp`), which writes a DACL for SYSTEM, Administrators and OWNER RIGHTS, and the key file inherits it.
- The runner's temp folder ACL contributes the ACE instead.
The `icacls` step added to the Windows sweep by almondy-columned-iguanodon prints the ACL of a fresh `mkdtemp` directory and a freshly minted key, which distinguishes these.

## Note on policy
Making the copy acceptable to OpenSSH means writing an owner-only DACL on it. The operator rejected that as part of option (1) on cloistered-decomposed-nymph (2026-11-18), which chose to rely on the default ACL. Whether rebar should write such a DACL anyway so that signing works on Windows, or declare op-cert signing unsupported on Windows, needs an operator decision.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The source of the OWNER RIGHTS ACE is identified from the sweep's `icacls` output and recorded here.
- [ ] Either op-cert signing composes and signs on a Windows runner (the tests in `openssh-key-acl.args` pass in a `sweep (windows)` run on main), or the operator's decision to leave it unsupported is recorded and the tests skip on Windows with that reason.
compiled_state.title: Windows: Win32-OpenSSH rejects the op-cert key copy (OWNER RIGHTS ACE), so signing cannot run on Windows
